## Cross-sensitisation

There is some research into cross-sensitisation between different substance addictions, such that one makes an individual more susceptible to another. Although this evidence is highly mixed and it may not be reasonable to assume sufficient variation in the present sample (predominantly highly educated students) I'll explore this in more detail below.

```{r}
data_params |>
  dplyr::select(contains("assist") & contains("total")) |>
  summary()
```

Assist questionnaire interpretation guidelines from the WHO, see https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/978924159938-2.

| Risk Level    | Alcohol | All Other Substances |
|---------------|---------|----------------------|
| Lower risk    | 0-10    | 0-3                  |
| Moderate risk | 11-26   | 4-26                 |
| High risk     | 27+     | 27+                  |

```{r}
#| label: fig-assist
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of low, moderate, and high risk of addiction across substances."
#| warning: false
#| out-width: "95%"

# define risk categories based on WHO cutoffs
categorize_risk <- function(score, substance_type) {
  if (substance_type == "alcohol") {
    case_when(
      score <= 10 ~ "Low risk",
      score <= 26 ~ "Moderate risk",
      score >= 27 ~ "High risk",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  } else {
    case_when(
      score <= 3 ~ "Low risk",
      score <= 26 ~ "Moderate risk",
      score >= 27 ~ "High risk",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  }
}

# create risk categories for all assist variables
assist_risk_data <- data_params |>
  dplyr::select(contains("assist") & contains("total")) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "substance", values_to = "score") |>
  drop_na(score) |>
  mutate(
    substance_clean = str_remove(substance, "assist_") |>
                     str_remove("_total") |>
                     str_to_title(),
    substance_type = if_else(str_detect(substance, "alcohol"), "alcohol", "other"),
    risk_category = map2_chr(score, substance_type, categorize_risk),
    risk_category = factor(risk_category, 
                          levels = c("Low risk", "Moderate risk", "High risk"))
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(risk_category))

# calculate risk for each substance
risk_proportions <- assist_risk_data |>
  dplyr::count(substance_clean, risk_category) |>
  dplyr::group_by(substance_clean) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    proportion = n / total,
    percentage = proportion * 100
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

# colour palette for risk categories
risk_colors <- c(
  "Low risk" = "#2E8B57",      
  "Moderate risk" = "#FF8C00",   
  "High risk" = "#DC143C"     
)

# prepare waffle data
waffle_data <- risk_proportions |>
  dplyr::mutate(scaled_n = round(proportion * 100)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(substance_clean = factor(substance_clean, 
                                  levels = c("Alcohol", "Amphetamine", "Cannabis", "Cocaine", "Hallucinogens",
                                             "Inhalants", "Opioids", "Sedatives", "Other")
  )) |>
  uncount(scaled_n) |>
  group_by(substance_clean) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # create x and y coordinates for each square
    y = rep(1:10, each = 10, length.out = n()),
    x = rep(1:10, length.out = n())
  ) |>
   dplyr::mutate(
    risk_category = factor(risk_category, 
                          levels = c("High risk", "Moderate risk", "Low risk"))) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

# create waffle plot
waffle_data |>
  dplyr::filter(substance_clean != "Other") |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = risk_category)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.25) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ substance_clean, ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual( 
    values = c("Low risk" = viridis(n = 1, option = "D", begin = .75, end = .75), 
               "Moderate risk" = viridis(n = 1, option = "B", begin = .85, end = .85), 
               "High risk" = viridis(n = 1, option = "B", begin = .5, end = .5)),
               
    drop = FALSE, 
    name = ""
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal() +  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "plain", size = 12),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(), # remove panel borders
    panel.background = element_blank(), # remove panel background
    plot.background = element_blank(), # remove plot background
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "plain", hjust = 0, size = 12)
  )
```

@fig-assist displays the proportion of high, moderate, and low risk of substance addictions for the different substances assessed as part of the ASSIST questionnaire. These cut-offs are based on those put forward by the WHO and, across the board, indicate very few instances of moderate or high risk. Thus, follow-up analyses on differences in substance don't make sense.
